title: Key invariants mu (potential) and pinv (p-adic) close IMO 2026 Problem 1
intent: Prove that IMO 2026 Problem 1's answer is `true` together with the full end-state characterisation (no infinite play, a terminal board exists, every terminal board has `bigCount` 1, and all terminal boards share the same `bigPart`) by carrying the whole proof on two conserved quantities: a potential `mu s = 2 * s.prod + bigCount s` that strictly decreases along every move, and a p-adic invariant `pinv p s` that pins the surviving entry's prime factorization.

parent.name: answer_correctness
parent.statement:
theorem answer_correctness
    (s₀ : Board)
    (h_card : Fact_card s₀)
    (h_all_gt1 : Fact_all_gt1 s₀)
    : answer = true ↔
        ( (¬ ∃ f : ℕ → Board, f 0 = s₀ ∧ ∀ k, Move (f k) (f (k + 1)))
          ∧ (∃ t, Relation.ReflTransGen Move s₀ t ∧ IsTerminal t)
          ∧ (∀ t, Relation.ReflTransGen Move s₀ t → IsTerminal t → bigCount t = 1)
          ∧ (∀ t₁ t₂, Relation.ReflTransGen Move s₀ t₁ → IsTerminal t₁ →
               Relation.ReflTransGen Move s₀ t₂ → IsTerminal t₂ →
               bigPart t₁ = bigPart t₂) )

applicability.goal_shape: A competition problem whose answer is a Boolean plus a characterisation of the end state of a terminating multiset-rewriting process, stated as an iff between `answer = true` and a conjunction (no infinite play, a terminal state exists, every terminal state has `bigCount` 1, and all terminal states share the same `bigPart`). The glue is carried by two conserved quantities: a potential `mu s = 2 * s.prod + bigCount s` that strictly decreases along every move, and a p-adic invariant `pinv p s` (the gcd of p-adic valuations of the entries) that pins the surviving entry's factorization.
applicability.use_when: the process is a finite rewriting system whose termination and confluence can both be shown from one potential and one invariant; the potential is a linear combination of a strictly-decreasing quantity and a bounded one (here 2 * prod plus bigCount); and the invariant factors through every prime, so equality of two end states follows from equality of all p-adic valuations.
applicability.avoid_when: the move does not change the potential monotonically (so descent needs a different measure); the invariant is too weak to distinguish the end states (so confluence needs a separate argument); or the end-state characterisation is not expressible as gcd/factorization facts already in the library (here `pinv` needs `Nat.factorization_gcd`, `Nat.factorization_lcm`, `Nat.factorization_div`, and the custom `gcd_min_sub`).

consequences: The move obliges the writer to (i) prove the potential strictly decreases along every move (`mu_lt_of_move`), a two-case analysis on whether `gcd m n = 1`; (ii) prove the invariant is preserved along a move and along its reflexive-transitive closure (`pinv_move`, `pinv_rtg`); (iii) prove positivity propagates along moves (`pos_of_move`) so the potential stays defined and non-negative; and (iv) lift the single-step facts to the reflexive-transitive closure by induction (`pos_rtg`, `pinv_rtg`) and to termination by well-founded induction on the potential (`exists_terminal_aux`). Failure mode: `mu` mixes a multiplicative quantity (`s.prod`) with an additive one (`bigCount`); if the move could increase the product while decreasing `bigCount`, a single potential would no longer be monotone and the two quantities would have to be tracked separately.
